answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal: a new agent publishes an onyx-hard hash of its keypair plus a small bond to a shared atlas of identities, then waits a full epoch before it may transact or grade. Each entry costs real capital and real time, so an attacker who wants a meadow of fake agents must lock bonds for all of them at once and wait together, and a collusion finding slashes every bond tied to the same reveal window.
